CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Sarah is a 27-year-old female presenting for her annual visit. She reports she has been doing better overall but has been struggling with depression on and off over the past year, particularly due to remote work and being confined indoors. She is currently taking Prozac 20 mg daily, which has helped her in the past. She feels that increasing the dose may help her through this current difficult period. She also reports chronic back pain that is managed but bothersome, particularly when sitting for long periods at her desk at work. Pain improves with movement and standing. She denies pain or tingling radiating down her legs but reports some mild numbness. She is able to perform activities of daily living, though symptoms are exacerbated by prolonged sitting or standing. She has a history of congenital coronary artery disease for which she underwent coronary artery bypass grafting at a young age. She reports her heart has been doing well and her arteries have been looking good.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain, dyspnea, or cardiac symptoms. Denies leg pain, weakness, or tingling. Reports mild numbness in legs that feels like "falling asleep." Reports chronic back pain with positional component. Otherwise unremarkable.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Depression
2. Chronic back pain
3. Congenital coronary artery disease status post coronary artery bypass grafting

MEDICATIONS
1. Prozac 20 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works remotely at a desk. Reports being sedentary due to remote work arrangements over the past year.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: No acute distress
Neck: No thyroid enlargement
Cardiovascular: 3/6 systolic ejection murmur, stable
Pulmonary: Lungs clear bilaterally
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender
Musculoskeletal: Pain to palpation of lumbar spine; decreased lumbar flexion; lower extremity strength intact; no edema

RESULTS
EKG: Basically unchanged from last year
Lumbar spine X-ray: Stable from last year

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Depression: Increase Prozac from 20 mg to 40 mg once daily. Patient agrees with dose increase.
2. Chronic back pain: Refer to physical therapy for symptom management. Patient declines pain medication at this time and prefers to start with physical therapy.
3. History of CABG with congenital coronary artery disease: Continue aspirin 81 mg daily. Order echocardiogram for continued monitoring. Continue current cardiac management.
